next_step: Closed - lost to direct OpenAI/Anthropic APIs; mark NRR, set re-engage reminder for 2026-08
notes:
Summary: Late-stage procurement that we could not convert — customer decided to use OpenAI (and small teams also evaluated Anthropic) for initial rollout. Primary reasons: simplicity of direct API, existing engineering familiarity, and credit/discount alignment.

Timeline / recent activity: 
- 2025-10-01: Lead captured via GA form, initial SDR outreach.
- 2025-10-10: Intro call (SDR) — described fintech use case (real-time customer support + compliance monitoring).
- 2025-11-12: Discovery call (AE Maya Chen, SE Liam Ortiz) — deep dive on throughput (2k QPS peak), latency target < 150ms p95, strict audit log requirements. Fireflies: ff_20251112_001.
- 2025-11-20: Shared architecture deck + cost model (drive: pricing deck).
- 2025-12-05: POC kickoff — small sandbox on Redwood hosted API, SE assisted. Jira INF-3421 opened for a KV-cache performance issue.
- 2026-01-18: Security review meeting — security asked about data residency and KMS options. Fireflies: ff_20260118_007.
- 2026-02-10: POC metrics: latency fine in our env; they reported integration friction with their platform pipelines.
- 2026-02-15: Internal procurement puts external AI spend on hold (budget freeze).
- 2026-02-20: Final decision call — procurement and engineering align to go with OpenAI direct API (and Anthropic for multi-vendor pilot). Reason cited: "faster integration, fewer moving parts, team already comfortable with OpenAI SDKs, and early volume discounts/credits available from OpenAI partner program." Gmail threads documenting this: thread-CA+abcd1234novaharbor.

Use-case & requirements notes: 
- Workload: high-throughput support assistant + indexing/rerank for regulatory docs.
- Latency target: p95 < 150ms for chat, burstable to 2k QPS.
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high; expected annual token volume large — needed predictable unit economics.
- Model preferences: open to open and closed models; preferred simple hosted endpoints early.
- Routing/fallback: wanted multi-region fallback and automatic model variant fallback during outages.
- Security/compliance: SR required SSO (SAML), audit logs, and EU data residency for certain regulated lines.

Why we lost: 
- Simplicity & brand: Engineering lead explicitly said vendor brand mattered; "we're shipping quickly and the OpenAI ecosystem reduces friction."
- Integration velocity: they perceived direct OpenAI/Anthropic APIs as less setup overhead compared to Redwood Dedicated/Private options.
- Internal champion: post-POC the internal product owner left the company and no new champion emerged — stalled momentum.
- Budget: procurement froze broad external AI commitments and opted for a lower-touch route with OpenAI credits.

Follow-ups & internal notes: 
- Sales outcome: Closed — lost to competitor (OpenAI primary). Mark as no-revenue for FY26.
- Recommended churn mitigation: calendar reminder for Aug 2026 to re-open conversation after their pilot (re-engage playbook: show cost delta vs direct API at volume, highlight fallbacks and SLAs).
- Feedback for product team: simplify onboarding/contract language for mid-market to reduce perceived friction vs direct API.

Stubs/links: Drive: pricing deck, security FAQ. Tickets: INF-3421 (performance), SEC-1982 (residency Qs).

AE comments: "Nice technical fit but lost to speed & brand. Good POC signals — keep on re-engage cadence once their pilot with OpenAI stabilizes."

SE comments: "Latency and throughput OK in our tests; their infra team prioritized minimal integration work. Recommend surfacing a quickstart that mirrors OpenAI SDK ergonomics."
